question: Should stored update.channel: "extended-stable" package installs receive default read-only startup and 24-hour npm availability hints after the throttle-marker defect is fixed?
rationale: Tests can prove the mechanics, but changing existing stored extended-stable configs from foreground/status-only behavior to startup network checks is a product and upgrade-policy choice.

options.title: Approve default read-only hints
options.body: Accept the compatibility change once the throttle-marker bug is repaired, relying on the existing package-only and no-auto-apply safeguards.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in
options.body: Keep the implementation direction but gate extended-stable startup hints behind an explicit operator setting or migration path.

options.title: Keep foreground/status only
options.body: Pause or close this PR and preserve the current extended-stable contract from the merged package-update support work.
